theory.title: Tiempos narrativos y secuenciación
theory.explanation: Para contar historias combina varios tiempos pasados. El past simple presenta los acontecimientos principales; el past continuous describe el contexto o una acción en progreso; el past perfect señala algo que ocurrió antes de otro momento pasado. Usa when y while para relacionar acciones, by the time para indicar que algo ya había ocurrido y after/before/as soon as para ordenar sucesos. Los conectores later, eventually, suddenly y in the end ayudan a que el relato sea fácil de seguir.
theory.tip: Fíjate en la función de cada estructura y en el contexto antes de elegir la forma verbal.

patterns.label: Past simple: acción principal terminada
patterns.pattern: Acción principal terminada: We arrived just before sunset.
examples:
Acción principal terminada: We arrived just before sunset.
→ Volvía caminando a casa cuando vi el cartel.

patterns.label: Past continuous: contexto o acción en curso
patterns.pattern: Contexto o acción en progreso: It was raining when we left.
examples:
Contexto o acción en progreso: It was raining when we left.
→ Para cuando llegamos, la tienda había cerrado.

patterns.label: Past perfect: acción anterior
patterns.pattern: Acción anterior a otra pasada: The train had already left.
examples:
Acción anterior a otra pasada: The train had already left.
→ Mientras esperábamos, empezó a nevar.

patterns.label: Past simple + past continuous: interrupción
patterns.pattern: Una acción interrumpe otra: I was walking when I heard a noise.
examples:
Una acción interrumpe otra: I was walking when I heard a noise.
→ Nunca había visto el mar antes de aquel viaje.

patterns.label: While + past continuous: simultaneidad
patterns.pattern: Dos acciones simultáneas: While I was waiting, I was reading.
examples:
Dos acciones simultáneas: While I was waiting, I was reading.
→ Finalmente, encontramos el andén correcto.

patterns.label: When + past simple: momento del suceso
patterns.pattern: Marca el momento de un suceso: When the lights went out, everyone stopped.
examples:
Marca el momento de un suceso: When the lights went out, everyone stopped.
→ De repente, alguien dijo mi nombre.

patterns.label: By the time: algo ya había ocurrido
patterns.pattern: La acción anterior ya se había completado: By the time we arrived, the film had started.
examples:
La acción anterior ya se había completado: By the time we arrived, the film had started.
→ Después de comprobar la ruta, nos pusimos en marcha.

patterns.label: After + past perfect: secuencia anterior
patterns.pattern: Primero ocurre la acción en past perfect: After we had eaten, we went out.
examples:
Primero ocurre la acción en past perfect: After we had eaten, we went out.
→ Por suerte, conseguimos coger el último autobús.

patterns.label: Before + past simple: orden de acciones
patterns.pattern: Ordena dos acontecimientos: I checked the map before we set off.
examples:
Ordena dos acontecimientos: I checked the map before we set off.
→ Al final, todo salió bien.

patterns.label: Conectores de secuencia
patterns.pattern: Usa suddenly, later, eventually y in the end para guiar al oyente.
examples:
Usa suddenly, later, eventually y in the end para guiar al oyente.
→ Fue una experiencia que nunca olvidaré.

content.passage: Last spring, I was travelling to a small town to visit a friend. I had checked the timetable the night before, but I had misunderstood the platform number. While I was looking for the right train, I noticed that the departure board had changed. By the time I reached the other platform, my train had already left. I felt annoyed because I had been looking forward to the visit. Fortunately, a station worker explained that another train was leaving in twenty minutes. I bought a coffee and called my friend to explain the delay. While I was waiting, an older woman asked me for directions. She had lost her ticket and was trying to find the information desk. I helped her, and we started talking. Eventually, we discovered that we were going to the same town. We shared a taxi from the station and arrived together. What had begun as a frustrating journey became a memorable afternoon.

items.prompt: Tell a story about a time when a plan went wrong.
items.modelAnswer: I was travelling to visit a friend when I realised I had taken the wrong train. I had checked the route, but I had read the platform number incorrectly. Eventually, I arrived late, but my friend was waiting for me.

items.prompt: Describe an unexpected event that became a positive experience.
items.modelAnswer: I was waiting for a bus when I met someone who was going to the same event. We started talking and discovered we had similar interests. In the end, we spent the whole afternoon together.

items.prompt: Talk about a memorable journey.
items.modelAnswer: Last summer, I went to the mountains with my family. We had planned the route carefully, but the weather changed. While we were looking for shelter, we found a small café where we met other hikers.

items.prompt: Describe what was happening when something important occurred.
items.modelAnswer: I was preparing dinner when the phone rang. My friend told me she had got a new job. I was delighted because she had been waiting for that news for months.

items.prompt: Tell a story using by the time and eventually.
items.modelAnswer: By the time I reached the station, the train had left. I was disappointed, but eventually I found another route and arrived only half an hour late.

items.prompt: Describe a time you helped someone during an unexpected situation.
items.modelAnswer: I was walking through town when I noticed a tourist looking confused. He had lost his map, so I showed him how to get to the museum.

items.prompt: Explain how you prepare to tell a story clearly.
items.modelAnswer: I think about the background first, then explain the main events in order. I use past continuous for the situation, past simple for key actions and past perfect for earlier events.

items.prompt: Describe a childhood memory that you still remember clearly.
items.modelAnswer: I was playing in the garden when my cousins arrived unexpectedly. We had not seen each other for months, so we spent the whole afternoon playing games.

items.prompt: Talk about a close call or a moment when you were lucky.
items.modelAnswer: I was cycling home when a car stopped suddenly in front of me. Fortunately, I was going slowly and managed to stop safely. I had never felt so relieved.

items.prompt: Describe how a difficult experience changed your plans.
items.modelAnswer: I had planned to study abroad, but I became ill just before leaving. After I had recovered, I changed my plans and applied for a course closer to home.

content.audioTranscript: Ben: What happened on your way to the interview? Sara: I was walking to the bus stop when I realised I had left my folder at home. Ben: What did you do? Sara: I called my sister, who was still at home, and asked her to bring it. By the time she arrived, the bus had gone. Ben: That sounds stressful. Sara: It was, but fortunately another bus came ten minutes later. While I was travelling, I checked the address again and noticed that I had written the wrong building number. Ben: Did you manage to find it? Sara: Yes. Eventually, a receptionist showed me the correct entrance. I arrived just in time, and the interview went well. Ben: What a morning! Sara: I know. In the end, everything worked out.
